todo_line: - [ ] 001 Implement and test the actor-bearing custom-group removal use case at the Club boundary, including custom-group/actor/target validation, self/last-member removal, idempotency, and reuse of `GroupMemberRemoved` without club/role removal.
outcome: Bring the existing unaccepted task-001 candidate to review-ready status by freshly validating the actor-authorized custom-group removal boundary on this source baseline and repairing only concrete task-001 gaps, if any.
scope: Inspect and preserve the existing candidate spanning Memba.Membership.remove_custom_group_member/1 and /2, the actor-bearing RemoveCustomGroupMember command, Club.execute/2 authorization and identity checks, Club-routed dispatch, and focused tests.

Confirm from current Club aggregate state that an active custom-group member may remove another member or themselves and that an active club.manage_members holder may remove a member while outside the group; ordinary or inactive outsiders must remain unauthorized.

Confirm exact typed club, custom-group, target membership/person, and actor identities are enforced, including rejection of actors or targets that are not active in the routed club and rejection of Everyone/Admin system groups.
Confirm self-removal and final-member removal are allowed, including an event-free exact retry after self-removal, with the custom group unchanged and the target still an active club member.

Confirm a real transition emits only the existing actor-free GroupMemberRemoved event and does not alter club membership, Admin role assignment, club.manage_members authority, invitations, or the trusted actor-free RemoveGroupMember path.
Add or adjust only focused task-001 tests when current coverage does not directly establish those rules; otherwise leave the candidate unchanged and return fresh passing evidence.
scope_exclusions: Do not implement follow cleanup, public Messaging API changes, or remove/re-add cleanup ordering; pending tasks 004-008 own that cross-context outcome.
Do not change conversation/query authorization, queued-delivery handoff, open LiveView refresh, or stale-view behavior; pending tasks 009-011 own those boundaries.
Do not add Leave/Remove controls, confirmations, shared member-row changes, former-member surfaces, or empty-group UI behavior.
Do not edit either iteration-064 acceptance feature file or remove its runner-debt tags in this packet.
Do not run dev check, dev check --quick, dev ci, the browser suite, or another full-suite command; the deterministic dev_check node and explicit final task 017 own iteration-wide validation.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 1 and the matching acceptance criteria require the actor-bearing Club-boundary removal use case, member/outside-admin authority, self and last-member removal, system-group guards, idempotency, and preservation of club membership and roles.
Current Membership writes use Club-owned event-sourced state for active membership and role decisions; projection preflight must not own the removal invariant.
Membership owns group membership state. This packet stays inside Membership and leaves follow cleanup to the later cross-context obligation.
The unaccepted candidate has a dedicated command with enforced club_id, group_id, membership_id, person_id, and actor_person_id fields.
The candidate exposes remove_custom_group_member/1 and /2 and builds the five-identity command. Existing remove_member/2 is club departure and must remain distinct.

RemoveCustomGroupMember currently validates routed and typed identities, custom-group status, current actor authority, and the exact active target. authorize_custom_group_removal_actor/2 includes an exact self-removal retry case; remove_custom_group_member_decision/2 emits GroupMemberRemoved or an empty retry.
The candidate registers RemoveCustomGroupMember on the Club route while retaining the separate trusted RemoveGroupMember command.

Current integration coverage exercises the sole emitted event and projection, ordinary retry, final-member self-removal, outside-admin removal with preserved Admin authority, outsider refusal, wrong targets, system groups, and required API attributes.
The RemoveCustomGroupMember authorization block covers aggregate-state member/manager authority, self-removal retry, identity mismatches, typed IDs, system groups, and unchanged club role state.
This test protects the actor-bearing public command versus trusted actor-free command/event shapes.
The candidate's command is included in both Membership App and Router registration assertions.

The current test explicitly loads Memba.Membership before asserting the new public exports and continued absence of a public remove_group_member API; this file changed after the prior worker's focused run and needs fresh evidence.
Follow the project Elixir and focused-test conventions; avoid timing sleeps and use start_supervised!/1 when starting test processes.

constraints: Treat the carried code as an unaccepted candidate, not accepted evidence; inspect it and return fresh validation from source baseline 15d75fd4ac9f439e847f6b0836aad3901b69b854.
Keep task identity 001 and candidate provenance intact; this is a normal implementation/revalidation attempt because no revise review verdict exists.
Do not authorize from projections or caller-supplied role claims; the current Club aggregate state owns actor, target, group, and permission decisions.
Do not broaden or replace the trusted actor-free RemoveGroupMember path used by system-group policies, replay, setup, or fixtures.
Do not add actor_person_id to GroupMemberRemoved; actor identity belongs to the command while the existing event remains the reusable membership fact.
No custom-group member floor exists. Removing the final member must not archive, delete, rename, or otherwise mutate the group.
Keep exact retries event-free, including a self-removal retry after the actor has ceased to be a group member.
Limit any edits to task-001 Membership implementation and focused tests; do not absorb pending follow, authorization, delivery, LiveView, UI, acceptance-feature, or final-gate work.

Report fresh exit statuses and test counts for both focused commands on the exact handoff state; do not rely on the prior worker's recorded runs.

Identify the assertions proving member removal, outside-manager removal without joining, ordinary/inactive outsider rejection, self and final-member removal, exact retry idempotency, routed-club actor/target validation, and system-group rejection.

Show that GroupMemberRemoved is the only event for a real transition and that club membership, Admin role/management permission, the custom group, and the trusted actor-free removal path remain intact.
Report git diff --check. If any focused failure cannot be repaired within task 001, return a concrete replan or human-blocked result instead of broadening scope or claiming completion.
